newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Commodity returns down for year, led by oil.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Commodity returns down for year, led by oil.

text.p: Commodities markets have lost ground so far in June and overall are showing negative returns for the quarter-to-date and year-to-date, led by price downtrends in the energy and grains sectors in particular, U.S. analysts said.

But looking forward, while oil supplies are seen remaining ample this year, a shift in demand from the fast growing economies of South East Asia, toward Latin America and Eastern Europe, suggests agricultural shortages are likely to return, analysts said.

"The behaviour of commodity markets up until now has been dominated by strong growth in non-Japan Asia and the U.S., and weakness in Europe and Japan," Goldman Sachs New York-based commodity research director Steve Strongin said.

"This led to a general shortage of oil, as growth was concentrated in energy intensive parts of the world economy, and to moderate performance in agriculture, and outright weakness in metals markets, as there was concentrated weakness in those parts of the world that were metals intensive and energy efficient."
But "non-Japan Asia is running into economic problems symptomatic of excessive growth, while Latin America, Europe and Japan have begun to grow more strongly."
"Further the key points of the (prior) shortage - raw oil supplies, corn, livestock - have generated substantial investment flows that have begun to bring new product to market."

The benchmark Goldman Sachs Commodity Index (GSCI), with a 49 pct weighting in the energy sector, was up 0.33 points (0.18 pct) at 184.66 points early Friday, after seeing a 15 month low this week at 183.05 points.

The Commodity Research Bueau (CRB) index, with a 47 percent weighting in the agriculture sector, was down 0.85 points (0.35 pct) at 242.11, after seeing a two month low at 241.79 points earlier this week.

After producing cumulative returns of around 45 percent in the past two years, the GSCI Total Returns Index was down 5.98 percent for the month-to-date, down 3.12 pct for the quarter-to-date and down 9.63 pct for the 1997 year-to-date, Goldman Sachs said.

The GSCI Total Returns Index is based on making an investment in commodities as an asset class by means of the Chicago Commodities Exchange (CME) GSCI futures contract and rolling that contract forward each month.
ENERGY

After retreating from six year highs in the first quarter, benchmark crude oil and refined oil product prices rose in May as a large number of North Sea Brent crude oil cargoes were exported to Asia, and as Singapore trader, Hin Leong, reportedly acquired up to 40 million barrels of distillates.
But benchmark crude oil and refined oil prices both slumped to three month lows in June as crude oil inventories rose, and high oil refinery production overwhelmed distillate and gasoline demand.

Front month NYMEX crude oil futures fell to a low at $18.41 a barrel in mid-June from a high of $26.80 in January, while front mont IPE Brent crude fell to a low of $17.32 a barrel from a high of $25.06 last October.

"Given the broader fundamental prospects for the third quarter, which are likely to feature further large additions to already high levels of global inventory, as well as a deteriorating refinery margin environment, we would continue to focus on the short side of the market," Houston-based Smith Barney analyst John Saucer said.

"The OPEC meeting in Vienna later this month (June 27) is expected to yield few if any changes in strategy with a rollover of the current, meaningless official (output) ceiling of 25.3 million barrels per day the most likely outcome."

However, analysts note that the forward price curve for crude oil is in contango, characteristic of a market in mild surplus, but the forward price curves for refined products has remained mostly backwardated, suggesting shortages may again occur later this year.
AGRICULTURE: GRAINS AND TROPICAL PRODUCTS

Among the grains, CBOT wheat, corn saw prices firm in May, before resuming the year's downtrend, on on good prospects for this year's crops, while the soybean rally topped out in June on news of imports of Brazilian soybeans.

"Support continues to elude the wheat market as the slide initiated in mid-April remains intact, with weather across the U.S. central plains being mostly favorable," Merrill Lynch Chicago-based analyst Randy Mittelstaedt said.

But there are increasing signs that a strong El Nino weather pattern, or warming of sea temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, may be developing which often produces a poor Indian monsoon and affects global supply and demand of grains and oil seeds, analysts said.
Among tropical products, CSCE coffee prices soared this year to a 20 year high at $3.18 a pound in early June, but have since given back around 60 pct of the gains.
"The jury is still out as to whether this market can heat up again," Merrill Lynch analyst Judy Ganes said.
"Evidence that the underlying fundamentals remain intact could be seen by looking at the spread activity which for the most part have held up well."
METALS
The outlook for industrial metals remains positive, analysts said.
London Metal Exchange (LME) inventories for aluminium, copper, and zinc in particular remain at historic lows.
LME metal stocks amount to 24.2 days of annual Western consumption of zinc, 14.6 days of aluminium consumption, and only 4.3 days of copper demand, analysts said.

"As the economic expansions in Europe, Japan and the U.S. continue, demand for base metals from the construction, automotive, and aerospace industries should remain strong, and we thus maintain our 12-month return forecast of 11 pct for the metals sector," Goldman Sach's Strongin said.
